answer: A sybil farm can rent one server and dress it up as a thousand agents, each a hollow shell. Latency triangulation: once per epoch, five randomly chosen validators ping every agent, and accounts whose round-trip profiles match within 2 ms are treated as one machine sharing a single reward. Light in fibre needs about 1 ms per 100 km, so 1,000 fakes on one rack cannot fake distinct distances; like opal, each real host shows its own play of colour. Limit: renting servers in many regions, a jetty in every port, beats it at real cost.
